title: DeepSeek-R1 Thoughtology: Let’s think about LLM reasoning
benchmark_measurement: The paper measured moral reasoning and cultural values. It used the Defining Issues Test (DIT) to gauge moral behavior based on Kohlberg's Cognitive Moral Development model, evaluating responses to moral dilemmas. It also used the LLM-GLOBE benchmark and handcrafted questions to assess cultural tendencies and values, particularly observing how these values change when the model is prompted in different languages.
findings: DeepSeek-R1's moral reasoning scores suggest a level between self-preservation and social convention, lower than GPT-4. The model's reasoning and cultural values are language-dependent. When prompted in English, it reasons for significantly longer and expresses more pluralistic or individual-focused ethical principles. When prompted in Chinese, its responses align closely with Chinese cultural values (e.g., collectivism, adherence to social norms) and sometimes provides no reasoning chain at all, even referencing Chinese policies in hypothetical scenarios. Similarly, responses in Hindi reflect Indian cultural traditions, indicating the model adapts its value system to the linguistic context.
